title: Sure
name: sure
description: Personal finance app for keeping your whole net worth in one place, with accounts, investments, budgets, transaction rules, CSV imports and reports, plus an optional AI assistant. A community fork of Maybe Finance. Source: https://github.com/we-promise/sure

env.name: SURE_SECRET_KEY_BASE
env.label: Secret key base (required)
env.description: Signs logins and encrypts saved bank and API credentials. Generate one with: openssl rand -hex 64. Keep it the same when you redeploy, or saved credentials can't be read.

env.name: SURE_DB_PASSWORD
env.label: Database password (required)
env.description: Generate one with: openssl rand -hex 32. Keep it the same when you redeploy, or Sure can't reach its database.

env.name: SURE_PORT
env.label: Host port for the web UI

note: Fill in both secrets before you deploy, since the stack won't start without them (openssl rand -hex 64 for the key base, openssl rand -hex 32 for the database), and keep them the same on every redeploy - the key base also encrypts saved bank and API credentials. Give it a minute on first start while it sets up the database, then open it on port 3400 and pick "create your account". The first account becomes the super admin. Sign-ups stay open after that, and everyone else gets their own separate household, so close them under Settings --> Self-Hosting --> Onboarding, or add SURE_ONBOARDING = closed (or invite_only) to the stack's environment variables and redeploy. Exchange rates and share prices come from Twelve Data with a free key, or switch both to Yahoo Finance (no key) on the same page, and the AI assistant wants an OpenAI-compatible key there too. Bank syncing is optional. A worker container runs imports, syncs and the scheduled jobs. Your data lives in Postgres, in the postgres-data volume, and uploads in sure-storage. Docs: self-hosting with Docker
